sequoiacap.com.name: Sequoia Capital
sequoiacap.com.note: London office since 2021 and 38 European deals in 24 months; the highest-signal US name on any European cap table.

a16z.com.name: Andreessen Horowitz
a16z.com.note: Largest US venture franchise; European activity is rising fast off a small base and skews AI and crypto.

lsvp.com.name: Lightspeed Venture Partners
lsvp.com.note: Dedicated European team out of London and Berlin; a regular lead in the AI and enterprise rounds Highland tracks.

generalcatalyst.com.name: General Catalyst
generalcatalyst.com.note: Absorbed La Famiglia and runs real London and Berlin teams; 10 percent of the portfolio is already European.

accel.com.name: Accel
accel.com.note: US mothership of the deepest European Series A franchise; 15.6 percent of deals are European, the richest Highland-stage feeder.

bvp.com.name: Bessemer Venture Partners
bvp.com.note: London office since 2021; European expansion-stage SaaS coverage overlaps Highland's entry point directly.

indexventures.com.name: Index Ventures
indexventures.com.note: SF seat of the London-born franchise; a third of the portfolio is European and it feeds Highland at A and B.

foundersfund.com.name: Founders Fund
foundersfund.com.note: Rare in Europe but decisive when present; defence and frontier-tech bets like Helsing set valuation benchmarks.

khoslaventures.com.name: Khosla Ventures
khoslaventures.com.note: Deep-tech and AI conviction investor; under 4 percent European, so a signal not a co-investor.

kleinerperkins.com.name: Kleiner Perkins
kleinerperkins.com.note: Storied franchise rebuilt around enterprise AI; European exposure stays thin at 4 percent of deals.

felicis.com.name: Felicis
felicis.com.note: Prolific early-stage AI and infra picker; European names are few but tend to be good ones.

nea.com.name: New Enterprise Associates (NEA)
nea.com.note: One of the largest US venture balance sheets; Europe is under 5 percent of activity and opportunistic.

benchmark.com.name: Benchmark
benchmark.com.note: Small, concentrated and rarely in Europe, but a Benchmark seat on a European board is the strongest early signal there is.

crv.com.name: CRV
crv.com.note: Early-stage enterprise and dev-tools specialist; barely 2 percent European, mostly a US signal.

initialized.com.name: Initialized Capital
initialized.com.note: Seed-stage generalist from the YC diaspora; negligible European footprint.

sparkcapital.com.name: Spark Capital
sparkcapital.com.note: Growth fund with a taste for category-defining consumer and infra; near 9 percent European including Klarna heritage.

usv.com.name: Union Square Ventures
usv.com.note: Thesis-driven NYC firm; roughly 10 percent European with a long networks-and-fintech memory.

insightpartners.com.name: Insight Partners
insightpartners.com.note: Software growth at industrial scale; 200 European portfolio companies and the buyer Highland meets in every process.

ycombinator.com.name: Y Combinator
ycombinator.com.note: 660 European companies through the program; the single biggest upstream source of Highland-stage US-flavoured European startups.

base10.vc.name: Base10 Partners
base10.vc.note: Automation-of-the-real-economy thesis with 13 percent of deals European; punches above its size in Highland-relevant sectors.

8vc.com.name: 8VC
8vc.com.note: Lonsdale's firm, HQ moved to Austin in 2020 with the SF office retained; defence and logistics tilt, thin in Europe.

redpoint.com.name: Redpoint
redpoint.com.note: Solid mid-size franchise across early and growth; under 3 percent European.

ivp.com.name: IVP
ivp.com.note: Late-stage venture with a London office since 2023; cheques above Highland's entry but a strong downstream signal.

iconiqcapital.com.name: ICONIQ
iconiqcapital.com.note: ICONIQ Growth's B2B software machine; 9 percent European and climbing, with a London presence and Highland-stage overlap.

coatue.com.name: Coatue
coatue.com.note: Crossover fund back on offence; 10 percent European and consistently prices the AI and fintech rounds above Highland.

thrivecap.com.name: Thrive Capital
thrivecap.com.note: Josh Kushner's concentrated franchise; few European deals but each one (Monzo, Lovable) resets the market.

greenoaks.com.name: Greenoaks
greenoaks.com.note: Concentrated growth bets with 11 percent of the book European; moves early and large when conviction lands.

tcv.com.name: TCV
tcv.com.note: London office since 2012; Revolut, Mollie and Trade Republic make it the US growth firm most embedded in European software.

sapphireventures.com.name: Sapphire Ventures
sapphireventures.com.note: Enterprise software growth with an SAP-anchored LP base and a London office since 2020; co-invests at Highland's stage.

battery.com.name: Battery Ventures
battery.com.note: Boston HQ with a London office since 2016; capital-efficient European software and industrial tech is core Battery territory.

summitpartners.com.name: Summit Partners
summitpartners.com.note: Boston growth equity with a dedicated Europe fund run from London; hunts the same capital-efficient software Highland does.

leftlanecapital.com.name: Left Lane Capital
leftlanecapital.com.note: Brooklyn growth firm with a real London seat; internet and consumer subscription growth, nearly a quarter of deals European.

generalatlantic.com.name: General Atlantic
generalatlantic.com.note: Global growth equity with 88 European portfolio companies and a large London office; the classic exit-round buyer above Highland.

tigerglobal.com.name: Tiger Global
tigerglobal.com.note: Slower than the 2021 blitz but still 84 European positions; when it re-accelerates it moves whole price levels.

addition.com.name: Addition
addition.com.note: Lee Fixel's fund; 13 percent European with a quiet, fast-moving style that preempts rounds Highland would want.

greylock.com.name: Greylock
greylock.com.note: Enterprise and security royalty; under 4 percent European, relevant as signal rather than co-investor.

meritechcapital.com.name: Meritech
meritechcapital.com.note: Late-stage software specialist (UiPath history); small team, sharp benchmarks, 7 percent European.

baincapitalventures.com.name: Bain Capital Ventures (BCV)
baincapitalventures.com.note: Bain's venture arm, now run from San Francisco; fintech and infra depth but under 4 percent European.

salesforceventures.com.name: Salesforce Ventures
salesforceventures.com.note: The most active CVC in European SaaS; 88 European positions and a frequent co-investor at Highland's stage.

bondcap.com.name: BOND
bondcap.com.note: Mary Meeker's growth fund; close to 10 percent European with a consumer-internet and marketplace tilt.

leadedge.com.name: Lead Edge Capital
leadedge.com.note: LP-network-driven growth equity; 10 percent European and shops exactly Highland's capital-efficient software profile.

stripes.co.name: Stripes
stripes.co.note: NYC growth equity across software and consumer; European activity is light at 5 percent of deals.

volitioncapital.com.name: Volition Capital
volitioncapital.com.note: Boston growth equity for bootstrapped software; thesis rhymes with Highland but only 2 of 100 deals are European.

dragoneer.com.name: Dragoneer Investment Group
dragoneer.com.note: Public-private crossover; 9 percent European, shows up late and large in the best software names.

psgequity.com.name: PSG
psgequity.com.note: Providence's growth arm with a dedicated PSG Europe fund out of London and Madrid; 21 percent of deals are European.

greathillpartners.com.name: Great Hill Partners
greathillpartners.com.note: Boston growth buyout for mid-market software and internet; 10 percent European, buys the companies Highland exits.
